solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poor Neil's spent endlessly, 6d

indicators.note: poor here means badly made or in a sorry state, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S, all five letters used as fodder

indicators.note: endlessly says the word spent loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Neil has been spending without stopping, and now he is broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; the definition is '6d', the answer to 6 down, BUST, in its sense of broke. NEILS plus SPEN (spent without its end) are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bust means having run out of money entirely, which is a synonym for being without a penny.

clue.text: Professor on board with bishop? Exactly

parts.note: Professor Plum is a suspect in the board game Cluedo (Clue in the US)
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A question about whether an academic sits on a committee alongside a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a committee, but it points to the board game Cluedo, whose suspects include Professor Plum.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb as an adverb means precisely or squarely, as in plumb in the middle.

clue.text: Pinch quick bites heading off to find bric-a-brac

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, informally to nick

indicators.note: heading off says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: quick bites are snacks

explanation.surface: Someone steals a few snacks before going out to look for curios.
explanation.definitionFit: Knick-knacks are small ornamental trinkets, the same assorted odds and ends as bric-a-brac; this spelling is a variant.

clue.text: Tipsy Indian gulps a beer mixed with it

indicators.note: gulps means swallows, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: IND is a standard abbreviation for Indian

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of a, beer and it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from India knocks back a beer with something in it and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' is not a nationality here but the abbreviation IND, and 'gulps' is the container signal rather than drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriated is a formal synonym for drunk, and tipsy means mildly drunk.

clue.text: In case silly wee runner appears

indicators.note: silly here suggests the word case is behaving foolishly, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: wee is informal for urine, also pee

explanation.surface: Just in case, a silly little runner turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like 'small' but is the noun for urine. 'silly' scrambles CASE into ESCA.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has run off from captivity, so a runner in the sense of a fugitive.

clue.text: Cut part of play featuring Arab briefly — this one?

definitions.text: Cut part of play featuring Arab briefly — this one?

indicators.note: featuring means including, so one piece is placed within the other
cut says the word for a part of a play loses its last letter

parts.note: a play is divided into acts and scenes

indicators.note: briefly says the word Arab is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A trimmed scene in a play has an Arab character; is he this kind?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a Saracen was the medieval name for an Arab, the very character the clue places in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim, so an Arab in a play could be one.

clue.text: 24 kept in small chest

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, which is BOOM
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Something is stored in a little chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom is a person's breast, the front of the chest.

clue.text: The other 6, 11, 21 and 1 across following 24?

parts.note: the clue words list several entries that all share one synonym: chest, financial ruin, a collapse and being broke, and the word that follows boom in the stock phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which word links the other answers and comes after the boom.
explanation.walkthrough: BUST means a bosom (6 across), bankruptcy (11), a crash (21) and penniless (1 across), and it pairs with BOOM (24) in 'boom and bust'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the cross-referenced words has bust as a synonym, and boom-and-bust is the familiar economic cycle.

clue.text: Several not always very old rounds at once

indicators.note: not says the word for always is taken out of the clue word several

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A rambling phrase about several old rounds fired at the same moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not always' means take EVER out of SEVERAL, leaving SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, many rounds fired together.

clue.text: US mothers take hours cooking fungi

indicators.note: cooking means being prepared or changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: moms is the American word for mothers

explanation.surface: American mothers spend hours in the kitchen preparing mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' scrambles MOMS and HOURS together. 'US' looks like the fodder but it labels the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are the edible fruiting bodies of certain fungi, so they are examples of the class.

clue.text: Cryptic clue about northern pawnbroker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
cryptic means puzzling or disguised, so the word clue is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cryptic clue about a northern moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' scrambles CLUE into ULCE, and 'about' puts that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is an old slang term for a pawnbroker, from the fiction that pawned goods were left with a relative.

clue.text: Young emperor, say, in Pitlochry's A-list

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A youthful emperor appears on the top guest list of the Scottish town of Pitlochry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young emperor' suggests a boy ruler; it is the emperor moth in its immature stage. Pitlochry is a town in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrysalis is the pupa of a butterfly or moth, so an emperor moth before it emerges is an example.

clue.text: By engaging steelmaker almost can, with time, spread 6d

indicators.note: engaging means taking in or holding, so one piece goes inside the other
spread means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged
almost says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Krupp was the famous German steelmaking firm

explanation.surface: A steel firm and a canning business go under together over time.
explanation.walkthrough: Krupp was a German steel and armaments firm. The definition is the answer to 6 down, BUST, meaning broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bust means becoming insolvent, the state of a business that cannot pay its debts.

clue.text: 24 leading pairs in the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: leading pairs means the first two letters of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: The front ranks of the Royal Artillery produce a loud bang.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 24 down, BOOM, in its sense of a deep loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom and a roar are both deep, loud, resonant noises, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Shortage of small vehicles — 100 seen moving in

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the word for vehicles

parts.note: cars are vehicles
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Few small cars are about, with only a hundred spotted on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes '100 seen' look like a count of cars; C is the Roman numeral and 'seen' is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarceness is the state of being in short supply, a direct synonym for a lack.

clue.text: 150 in eastern part of basilica in Vatican for example

indicators.note: in says the number is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: the nave is the main central part of a church
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people sit in the east end of a great Roman church.
explanation.walkthrough: Note the setter's slip: the nave is the western body of a church, but E simply means eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly surrounded by another country, as Vatican City is by Italy.

clue.text: One-time Arafat group is upset about report

parts.note: ex- means former, one-time
the PLO, Palestine Liberation Organization, was led by Yasser Arafat

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A former Palestinian group is unhappy about a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can mean a loud bang, such as a gunshot or blast, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: It's not on to back Tory and leader of opposition

indicators.note: to back means to turn backwards, so the word for Tory is reversed

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: leader of means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Backing the Conservatives and the opposition leader is simply not possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like 'support', but here it reverses CON to NOC.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal way of saying something is impossible, which is what not on means.

clue.text: Scrubbed if sick getting up in nude in bad form

indicators.note: in says the reversed pieces go inside the rearranged word
in bad form says the letters of nude are out of shape and rearranged
getting up in a down clue means rising, so the letters read upwards in reverse

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone cancelled plans because they were ill, rising unclothed and in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'getting up' reads the pieces upwards, which is backwards; the second 'in' belongs to the phrase 'in bad form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubbed in the sense of cancelled means annulled or made void, a synonym.

clue.text: Have bodyguard pursue gang

indicators.note: pursue means follow, so the bodyguard comes after the gang

parts.note: a posse is a group or gang of people
the SS began as Hitler's personal bodyguard

explanation.surface: A guard sets off in pursuit of a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, the same as to have it.

clue.text: Russian boss doesn't start split, say, using scorn

indicators.note: doesn't start says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the tsar was ruler of Russia

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a chasm is a deep split or cleft

explanation.surface: A Russian leader who will not open the split shows contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: CHASM is said with a hard K, so it sounds like CASM, the ending of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is mocking, contemptuous language, so it expresses scorn.

clue.text: It's oddly square and more than needed

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the following word

parts.note: plus means and, as in two plus two

explanation.surface: Something both strangely square and excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount left over beyond what is required, an excess.

clue.text: Wrong American reserves introduced bear

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the pieces go inside the word for wrong

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
US is the United States, American
TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer army reserve

explanation.surface: Wrongly brought-in American reserves endure.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) was the British Army's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a loss or injury is to suffer or bear it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: One left suspended in the past

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter for one goes from the other word

parts.note: on ice means put on hold, suspended
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single item was left hanging some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' is the phrase ON ICE, meaning postponed; removing I leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time, a synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Dramatic fall in credit has dissipated

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters of has are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp drop in credit has ruined someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a sudden collapse, as of a market or share price.

clue.text: Duke of Milan's not fully with it at end of day 24

indicators.note: not fully says the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest

indicators.note: at end of means take the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's duke is not quite with it at the close of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 24 down, BOOM, in its sense of a period of economic growth.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic boom is a time of flourishing wealth, the same as a period of affluence.

clue.text: Supply amount of energy from 14 down

definitions.meaning: to supply or give up, as a field gives a crop
the energy released by an explosion, often measured in kilotons for a bomb

explanation.definitionFit: Yield means both to produce or provide and the explosive force released by a bomb.

clue.text: Show contempt for money in time of 22

parts.note: to boo is to jeer at someone
M is the abbreviation for money in economics, as in M1

explanation.surface: Jeer at money at a time of plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a period of rapid economic growth and affluence.

clue.text: 6 across friend retired at a Roman institute

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: I is a standard abbreviation for institute; that the letters also run backwards through the printed words is a coincidence of this charade, since institute gives only its initial

explanation.surface: A close friend has withdrawn to a college in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read a hidden word with no indicator; it is a charade with I for institute, all turned by 'retired'. The definition leans on 6 across, BOSOM: a bosom friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover, a very intimate companion.

clue.text: Send away English team to centre in Anglesey

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a football or cricket team

indicators.note: centre in means take the middle letters of the following word

explanation.surface: An English side goes to the centre of the Welsh island of Anglesey.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglesey is an island off north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them from their country.

clue.text: Hebrew prophet's human failing

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: failing means going wrong, so the letters of human are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Old Testament prophet shows a human weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' looks like a noun, a flaw, but signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is a minor prophet of the Old Testament with a book named after him.

clue.text: Doctor welcomes any team with range of skills

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A doctor takes on any team that has varied abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Many-sided describes someone versatile, with many talents.
